learning_outcomes.text: Has basic knowledge of electricity distribution and selection of main elements of electrical networks.
Has theoretically supported and structured knowledge in the field of designing power supply systems for facilities with high power demand.
Has useful knowledge in the field of specialized issues of industrial electrical installations operation.
Is able to acquire information from literature and apply it in selecting basic elements of electrical networks and installations.
Is able to work individually and in a team in the implementation of a design task.
Is able to prepare documentation for the subject design task and a text containing a description of the solved problem.
Understands the need for continuous learning by monitoring current changes in the principles of electrical installation design.

syllabus_topics: Design of power and lighting installations for an industrial plant with assumed parameters. The project should include the following elements: 1. Initial assumptions. Selection of supply network voltage and distribution network. 2. Determination of power demand for power circuits. 3. Selection of supply network voltage and distribution network. 4. Determination of the location of the transformer station supplying the plant. 5. Selection of transformers. 6. Determination of capacitor bank power in the plant's departmental stations. 7. Selection of medium and low voltage network cables. 8. Determination of peak power of a selected industrial plant facility. 9. Calculations of lighting intensity in selected rooms. Determination of the number of lighting points. 10. Selection of cable cross-sections and cable protection for the facility's installation. 11. Electrical diagrams of power and lighting installations.

Introduction to industrial network issues. Electrical energy in industry. Characteristic features of industrial plants. Features of power supply systems and internal distribution networks. Tasks and requirements for industrial networks. Characteristic values of load diagrams.
Characteristics of receivers used in industry. Classification of lighting and power receivers in industrial plants. Characteristics of receivers and analysis of their impact on the network.

Problems of electrical energy quality. Impact of quality on receiver operation. Determination of voltage fluctuations and voltage curve distortion during operation of disturbing receivers. Methods and means of limiting voltage deviations and fluctuations.
Principles of technical and economic analysis. Components of annual costs. Methods of accounting for reliability costs.

Methods for determining peak power demand. Concept of peak power. Statistical and analytical methods for determining loads of switchgears, transformer stations, and industrial plants. Determination of power demand for power and lighting loads.

Design of power supply systems for industrial plants. Factors influencing the selection of the power supply system. Factors influencing the selection of voltage in the power supply system. Determination of the location of transformer-distribution stations. Selection of transformers.
Design of internal distribution networks. Principles of voltage selection in distribution and reception networks. Network systems. Principles of network system selection.
Optimization of industrial network structures. Structures of industrial electrical power networks. Selected methods for designing and optimizing network operation.
Methods for limiting short-circuit currents in industrial networks. Characteristics and comparison of limiting methods. Influence of electric motors on short-circuit values.

Reactive power compensation and optimization of reactive power source placement. Selection of reactive power compensation devices in an industrial network. Optimization of capacitor bank placement in radial and backbone networks.
Shock protection in electrical power networks. Technical means of basic and additional protection in networks up to 1 kV. Protection means in high voltage equipment.
